facts.text: For a vehicle on a uniform surface, the longitudinal motion equation is m·dv/dt = −F_brake − F_rolling − m·g·sin θ.
facts.quote: For a vehicle on a uniform surface the longitudinal equation is m·dv/dt = −F_brake − F_rolling − m·g·sin θ.

facts.text: If braking force were limited purely by a tire-ground coefficient proportional to normal load, mass terms would largely cancel and a heavy machine would stop in the same distance as a light vehicle.
facts.quote: If braking force were limited purely by a tire-ground coefficient proportional to normal load, the mass terms would largely cancel and a heavy machine would stop in the same distance as a light one.

facts.text: Real earth-moving machine brakes have finite torque and thermal capacity, breaking the idealized assumption under which heavy and light vehicles have the same stopping distance.
facts.quote: brakes have finite torque and thermal capacity

facts.text: Payload changes axle or track loads and the center of gravity of real earth-moving machines, breaking the idealized assumption under which heavy and light vehicles have the same stopping distance.
facts.quote: payload changes axle or track loads and the center of gravity

facts.text: Available ground shear for real earth-moving machines is nonlinear in load and slip, breaking the idealized assumption under which heavy and light vehicles have the same stopping distance.
facts.quote: the available ground shear is nonlinear in load and slip

facts.text: Rolling and sinkage resistance can be large for real earth-moving machines, breaking the idealized assumption under which heavy and light vehicles have the same stopping distance.
facts.quote: rolling and sinkage resistance can be large

facts.text: The propulsion system of a real earth-moving machine may take part in deceleration, breaking the idealized assumption under which heavy and light vehicles have the same stopping distance.
facts.quote: the propulsion system may take part in deceleration

facts.text: NIOSH's underground-haulage stopping formulation models front and rear normal loads, weight transfer, brake torque, rolling resistance, grade, and rotational inertia, with brake torque depending on actuation, velocity, and temperature.
facts.quote: NIOSH's underground-haulage stopping formulation therefore models front and rear normal loads, weight transfer, brake torque, rolling resistance, grade, rotational inertia, and a brake torque that depends on actuation, velocity and temperature.
